text: A9 still fails after removing test_quality from the parsed JSON: the raw-output scanner treats every "object_type" line as a metrics row, including the new procedure/codeunit rows. Restrict the scan to metrics; keep frozen outputs unchanged.
evidence: Confirmed (ledger P17): the scan at :543-569 runs over the whole stdout, and the fixture's [Test] TestSomething makes procedures non-empty. Design v2 'Where it lives' gives the legacy test two edits: remove top-level test_quality from the parsed value, and break the raw scan at the line "findings": [. Frozen legacy.* files unchanged. Acceptance row A13 proves edit 2 is needed (revert it alone -> red). Same as O1.

text: A1-A9 do not enforce traversal completeness. Empty visitor arms could compile and pass: nested control-flow asserts, expression-contained asserts and descent through AssertError are untested. Parameter receivers and AreNearlyEqual are also unpinned.
evidence: Confirmed (P18): exhaustiveness alone does not force recursion. Design v2 adds A10 (one assert per slot: if then/else, case branch/else, while, repeat, for, foreach, nested block, inside asserterror; break = empty each arm in turn -> count drops), A11 (in-body #if, both arms), A9 (parameter receiver; break = drop params from lookup), and AreNearlyEqual in A3 (break = drop it from the method list -> total 8). Asserts inside conditions/expressions cannot occur in valid AL (the assert methods return nothing); the expression recursion is stated as defensive, and A10 pins that a nested non-assert call in an assert's argument is not counted. Round 2 (re-raised): confirmed (P23) the lowerer flattens live in-body #if branches into plain statements (lower/mod.rs:2367-2387) and never builds BlockItem::Preproc, so A11 could not test that arm. Design v3: A11 kept as a binary test of the flattened behaviour (both arms count) and labelled as such; new U1 builds a Preproc block by hand with the public Ir::add_block and breaks the arm (empty -> 0, first branch only -> 1); rule 6 states which path real AL takes.

text: A1 checks identity-key presence, not the promised exact join with metrics. A wrong/null routine_id or wrong object metadata can pass. Compare every procedure's identity fields against exactly one metrics row at (path, line), including missing-app/nested-app null cases.
evidence: Design v2 A1: for every procedure row, exactly one metrics row has the same (path, line), and object_type, object_name, object_id, procedure_name, routine_id are equal, including routine_id null for a nested-app test; object_stable_id checked by value and null for nested app. A1b runs analyze-json-noapp: routine_id, object_stable_id, assert_count_reachable, zero_assert all null. Breaks: routine_id None, object line as line, unfiltered guid. Round 2 (re-raised): confirmed (P24) analyze-json-noapp has no [Test], so A1b was vacuous. Design v3: new fixture analyze-test-quality-noapp with two [Test] procedures (existing fixture untouched); A1b asserts exactly 2 rows, null routine_id/object_stable_id/assert_count_reachable/zero_assert per procedure, and null assert_count_reachable and zero_assert_procedures on the codeunit and workspace rows (O11 rule).

text: Performance comparison is underspecified: P16 measures CSV, while the consumer needs JSON. Benchmark base/new binaries with identical profile, format, dependencies and cache conditions.
evidence: Confirmed: P16 used --format csv (no graph) on a target/cdo binary. Design v2 measurement plan: master 60434aef vs branch, both --profile release-fast, same machine, no .alpackages, one discarded warm run, 5 runs each of --analyze --format json, median reported. P16 marked not a valid baseline. Same as O6.

text: The conditional object-key fallback cannot be done by a serde rename: renaming numeric object_id does not produce <appId>/Codeunit/N.
evidence: Correct: object_id is i64 (src/analysis.rs:22); the string comes from ids::encode_object_id (src/engine/ids.rs:177). Operator answer 2 settles it: Design v2 adds object_stable_id on procedure and codeunit rows, built with encode_object_id(guid, ir_object_type, ir_object_key), null when the object part of routine_id is null. The fallback now covers casing only.

text: Documentation plan covers CHANGELOG but omits README discoverability.
evidence: README.md:48-51 lists what --analyze reports. Design v2 'Where it lives' adds 'test assert counts (JSON)' there. Same as O8.

text: A9 says the legacy test stays green once it drops test_quality from the parsed Value. It will not: the raw stdout scan treats any "object_type" line as a row start; key-order (:553) and row_count (:565) asserts fail.
evidence: Confirmed (P17). Same fix as S1: two edits to the legacy test (drop the key from the parsed value; stop the raw scan at "findings": [), frozen files unchanged, A13 proves edit 2 is needed.

text: Rule 6 makes StmtKind exhaustive but blocks hold BlockItems; in-body #if (BlockItem::Preproc) is not covered and the both-arms policy is unstated. complexity_stmt ends in _ => {} and must not be the model; list every expression slot.
evidence: Confirmed (P18: stmt.rs BlockItem::{Stmt, Preproc}, complexity_stmt _ => {}). Design v2 rule 6: exhaustive match on BlockItem (Preproc visits every branch; an assert in both arms counts twice) and on StmtKind with no catch-all, listing every slot (assignment target/value, call, if cond/then/else, case scrutinee/patterns/bodies/else, while cond/body, repeat body/until, for var/from/to/body, foreach var/iterable/body, with receiver/body, try body/catch, asserterror block, exit value, block; explicit empty arms for break/continue/unknown). Does not copy complexity_stmt. A11 pins in-body #if (break: first branch only -> 1 -> red). Round 2 (re-raised): that break could not apply, because the lowerer flattens in-body #if (P23). Design v3 rule 6 states the real path (live branches flattened to statements, both arms count, dead nested branches absent) and moves the Preproc-arm proof to synthetic-IR unit test U1; A11 now documents the flattened behaviour only. Same fix as S2.

text: A this.Assert.AreEqual(..) receiver is Member{Identifier("this"), "Assert"}, not a bare name, so it is not counted. Accept this.<name> against globals, or state it as a limit.
evidence: Confirmed (P20: this lowers to Identifier("this"), receiver.rs:2357-2364). Design v2 rule 2 accepts this.X looked up in object globals only. A8 pins it (break: remove the this. arm -> red).

text: Database::"Customer" (ExprKind::DatabaseReference) is a compile-time constant but the spec classes it as an expression.
evidence: expr.rs:50-51 confirms the kind. Design v2 rule 5 counts DatabaseReference as literal_expected. A3 fixture includes AreEqual(Database::Customer, ..); literal total 6.

text: The expected CDO test count is exactly 1844, not 1844-1847: three grep hits are commented-out // [Test] lines.
evidence: Confirmed (P21): CDOOpenDocumentsTests.Codeunit.al:312, CDOSendCustStatementTests.Codeunit.al:244,401. Measurement plan v2 expects exactly 1844; any other number is a bug.

text: The 44.2 ms baseline came from a target/cdo binary that predates #159 and ran --format csv (no graph). Measure master vs branch with --format json, same profile, same machine.
evidence: Confirmed: binary mtime 2026-10-22 06:15, #159 (809fe684) committed 2026-10-23 13:55; its CSV header has no #159 fields. P16 marked invalid; measurement plan v2 as in S4.

text: The A2 break 'count any X.M() as an assert' only fails if the zero-assert test contains a non-assert member call; 'only setup code' does not guarantee one.
evidence: Design v2 A2: the zero-assert test's body is Rec.Init(); Rec.Insert(); so the break turns it red.

text: The README lists what --analyze reports; the plan updates the CHANGELOG only.
evidence: Same as S6: Design v2 adds 'test assert counts (JSON)' to README.md:50-51.

text: 130000 = Assert and 130002 = Library Assert are not verified here (no .alpackages). Confirm from the BC sidecar's symbols, or cut the numeric form.
evidence: Not cheaply verifiable (P22): the BC sidecar is stopped and reports 'exited unhealthy'; no test-library .app on disk; CDO uses the numeric form 0 times. Per operator, the numeric form is cut: Design v2 non-goals and rule 2 match by name only (assert / library assert); CHANGELOG states the limit.

text: Workspace membership is not actual same-app membership: nested apps also have declarations, so their helpers pass the DeclEntry filter. Filter by actual app-root membership.
evidence: Confirmed (P26): the source root walks nested apps (provider.rs:31-47) and #159 treats a nested-app file as another app (analysis.rs:291-295). Design v3 rule 7: a target is followed only if its declaration's file has the same app root as the test's file (deepest folder with app.json, else project root; a helper next to in_nested_app). A14: a root test calling a nested-app helper with 1 assert gets 0, precondition fan_in >= 1 on the helper; break (drop the root comparison) -> 1 -> red. CHANGELOG states 'same app' with this meaning. Round 3 (sol re-raise): the call map is keyed by (caller app root, RoutineNodeId) so a root and a nested declaration sharing one id keep their outgoing calls apart; fixture A14b with a break (key by id alone -> counted).

text: Reachability uses RoutineNodeId, but A7's two conditional declarations share that id; their outgoing edges merge and declaration-specific counts have no multiplicity policy.
evidence: Confirmed (P25): source_routine_node_id has no location or preprocessor context (sig_fp.rs:155-166); updater.rs keeps decl_multiplicity for this. Design v3 rule 7: a callee id's own count is the SUM over its declarations; a test contributes only its own declaration's count and its id seeds the visited set; a split test reaches the union of both arms' callees (stated limit). A7 hand values: arm 1 reachable 4, arm 2 reachable 5, split-helper caller U 3, precondition shared routine_id; breaks: own count as id sum -> 6, last-wins map -> U 2. Same as O10.

text: A4's break need not fail: every positive own count already has zero_assert == false, so excluding zero rows changes no assert sum. Mutate a real summand or omit a positive-count procedure.
evidence: Correct: with resolved counts, assert_count > 0 implies zero_assert == false, so the old break changed nothing. Design v3 A4 break: leave the last procedure of each codeunit out of the codeunit sums; precondition asserts that procedure has assert_count > 0 and assert_count_reachable > 0, so computed-sum and hand-total checks go red.

text: Removing the visited guard on the H<->H2 cycle can hang, not return '4+'. Separate cycle termination from the duplicate-count mutation; the binary runner blocks in .output().
evidence: Correct: without any guard the H->H2->H walk never ends. Design v3 A12(a) uses O12's variant: per-path guard plus every call edge counted; T's two call sites to H each give 1 + 2, so T = 6 instead of 3, red without looping. All listed breaks terminate, so no runner timeout is needed (stated). Same as O12.

text: Matching routine rows does not prove error-free parsing; recovery can keep declarations while dropping body calls. Parse fixtures explicitly and assert parse_incomplete == false.
evidence: Correct: parse_incomplete is node.has_error() per routine (lower/mod.rs:2107), independent of the declaration surviving. Design v3: the test member parses every .al file in both new fixtures with al_syntax::parse (already used by integration tests, e.g. tests/cli/cli_numberless_object_ids.rs) and asserts at least one object and parse_incomplete == false for every routine.

text: RoutineNodeId is not unique per declaration: same-signature declarations in #if arms share one id, edges are keyed by it, and 'own count of every other visited routine' is undefined for two declarations. State SUM, pre-mark the test's id, give A7 hand values.
evidence: Confirmed (P25). Same fix as S8: SUM over declarations for callee ids, test's own declaration only with its id pre-visited, union-of-callees stated, A7 hand values (4, 5, U 3) with two discriminating breaks.

text: zero_assert_procedures counts only true, so without a graph codeunit and workspace report a made-up 0. Give it the same null rule and assert it in A1b.
evidence: Correct. Design v3 field rules: zero_assert_procedures is null if any of its procedures has zero_assert null, else the count of true. A1b asserts null on the codeunit and workspace rows; break (old count-only-true rule) -> workspace 0 -> red.

text: The 'drop the visited set' break hangs on the H->H2->H cycle. Use a path-guarded per-edge count: T gives 6, not 3.
evidence: Correct. Design v3 A12(a) adopts this variant exactly; same fix as S10.
